newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi throws down gauntlet to hard left.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi throws down gauntlet to hard left.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi threw down a gauntlet to his troublesome hard left ally Communist Refoundation on Thursday, saying the party had to back his programme if it supported him in a confidence vote.

Addressing the Senate at the start of a debate on the future of his 11-month-old government, he said he needed a strong, cohesive majority to see through a programme that included tackling difficult reforms to the welfare state.
"It must be clear to everyone who supports this government and what its majority is," Prodi said.
"And it must equally be clear that whoever gives us their confidence today must share the wide-ranging programme we have worked on and which we now want to bring to fruition," he said.

His remarks were a clear reference to Refoundation, whose refusal to back Prodi in a vote on Wednesday on sending an Italian-led security force to Albania has confronted the prime minister with the most difficult crisis since he took office.

Refoundation, which holds the balance of power in the lower house, is diametrically opposed to many of Prodi's key economic policies but has said it intends to vote for him in confidence tests in the Senate later on Thursday and in the lower house.
